subject: pharmacology
title: Local anaesthetics: esters, amides and regional blocks

steps.tx: **Local anaesthetics** block voltage gated **sodium channels** from inside the nerve fibre membrane. The block shows **use dependence**, because rapidly firing fibres expose the binding site more often. Small pain and temperature fibres fail before larger motor fibres, so analgesia appears before paralysis. Inflamed acidic tissue traps the charged drug outside the fibre and it resists blockade. Cocaine alone constricts vessels, while every other agent in this class dilates vessels locally.
steps.say: Local anaesthetics block voltage gated sodium channels from inside the nerve fibre membrane itself. The block shows use dependence because rapidly firing fibres expose the binding site more often. Small pain fibres fail before motor fibres so analgesia appears before any paralysis develops. Inflamed acidic tissue traps the charged drug and it resists blockade in abscesses.

steps.tx: **Esters** and **amides** differ in metabolism, allergy risk and clinical behaviour in patients. Plasma cholinesterase hydrolyses esters quickly, and the resulting **PABA** metabolite explains most true allergy in this group. The liver metabolises amides such as lignocaine, bupivacaine and ropivacaine, and true allergy to amides stays rare. Bupivacaine carries the greatest cardiotoxicity after accidental intravenous injection, while ropivacaine separates sensory block from cardiac risk more safely. Prilocaine can cause methaemoglobinaemia in susceptible patients.
steps.say: Esters and amides differ in metabolism and allergy risk in ways that examinations test repeatedly. Plasma cholinesterase hydrolyses esters quickly and the PABA metabolite explains most true allergy cases. The liver metabolises amides such as lignocaine and ropivacaine and true allergy remains rare. Bupivacaine carries the greatest cardiotoxicity after accidental intravenous injection in clinical practice today.

steps.tx: Adding **adrenaline** prolongs a block, reduces surgical bleeding and reveals accidental intravascular injection early. A test dose that enters a vein produces tachycardia and it warns the anaesthetist immediately. Traditional teaching avoids adrenaline in **end artery** areas such as digits, penis, nose tip and earlobes, because vasoconstriction can cause tissue necrosis there. Cocaine remains the only local anaesthetic that constricts vessels by itself. Blanching with pain warns that perfusion has become critically poor.
steps.say: Adding adrenaline prolongs a block and it reduces surgical bleeding in the operative field. A test dose that enters a vein produces tachycardia and it warns the anaesthetist immediately. Traditional teaching avoids adrenaline in end artery areas because vasoconstriction can cause tissue necrosis there. Cocaine remains the only local anaesthetic that constricts vessels by itself without additives.

steps.tx: **Local anaesthetic systemic toxicity** begins with perioral numbness and tinnitus before seizures appear. Severe toxicity then produces arrhythmias and cardiovascular collapse that can kill the patient quickly. Treatment secures the airway, controls seizures with benzodiazepines and gives **20 percent intralipid** as a lipid sink. Prevention aspirates before injection, uses fractional doses and respects maximum safe limits always. Spinal anaesthesia below the second lumbar level causes sympathetic block and hypotension, which fluids and vasopressors treat.
steps.say: Local anaesthetic systemic toxicity begins with perioral numbness and tinnitus before seizures appear suddenly. Severe toxicity then produces arrhythmias and cardiovascular collapse that can kill the patient. Treatment secures the airway and it controls seizures with benzodiazepines in hospital. Clinicians give intravenous lipid emulsion promptly because the lipid phase extracts the drug. Prevention aspirates before injection and it respects maximum safe dose limits always.

steps.tx: This sagittal image shows a **subarachnoid needle** entering below the **conus medullaris**, which ends near the first or second lumbar level. The needle passes through supraspinous and interspinous ligaments and then through the tough ligamentum flavum. It finally enters the subarachnoid space among cauda equina roots, where hyperbaric local anaesthetic spreads within cerebrospinal fluid. Choosing the third to fourth lumbar space protects the cord, and sympathetic block at that level explains the vasodilatation and hypotension that follow.
steps.say: This sagittal image shows a subarachnoid needle entering below the conus medullaris in the lumbar spine. The needle passes through the ligaments and it enters the space among cauda equina roots. Hyperbaric local anaesthetic spreads within cerebrospinal fluid and it blocks the nerve roots there. Choosing a low lumbar space protects the cord from direct needle injury during the procedure.
